projects.title: Modeling and Optimizing the Third Stage of a Multi-Stage Rocket for Near-Orbit Altitude Using Classical Mechanics
projects.description: This project revolved around optimizing the third stage of the PSLV rocket to improve fuel efficiency, thrust stability, and trajectory control during orbital insertion. The idea came from analyzing limitations in traditional multi-stage rockets and applying theoretical modeling to overcome them. I used Tsiolkovsky’s rocket equation to simulate velocity changes over burn time, accounting for fuel mass, thrust, and gravitational losses. I also explored alternative engine types and tested them within the same parameters to evaluate performance differences. A Laval nozzle model was included to assess flow characteristics. The project concluded with a working text-based simulation.

projects.title: Extended STEM project using a generative artificial intelligence-powered UAV drone system
projects.description: This project is a fully autonomous UAV with integrated object detection and avoidance software, designed to detect obstacles and move toward the next open space while always returning to the displacement line between two preset coordinates. The concept originated after watching Roland Sigwart’s MIT lecture on flying robots. The coordinates, represented in (x, y) in 2D, are mapped either prior to or during flight, and the Cartesian coordinate system has been projected onto an oblate spheroid to represent the Earth. The sensor beneath the drone and the mapping of flight coordinates have been developed, the drone’s frame has been built, and the math for propeller tilt while maintaining stability has been completed with few errors.

projects.title: Ultrasonic Radar Based Obstacle Detection and Relay System for Autonomous Aerial Vehicles
projects.description: This project began during a 2024 summer engineering program at Oxford, where I developed an ultrasonic radar system to demonstrate sensor principles to younger students. To make the system more accessible, I replaced hidden wireless transmission with a visible LCD output. After completing the prototype, I integrated the upgraded system into my ongoing autonomous UAV project to improve real-time object detection and motor control. The LCD was removed, and data was rerouted through a Raspberry Pi to communicate with ESP32 boards managing drone movement. The radar sensors scan the environment while rotating on the y-axis and transmit obstacle data to influence drone navigation dynamically, based on preset mapping and sensor range limits.

projects.title: 6DOF Bionic Arm with Real Time Hand Tracking and Sensor-Based Control
projects.description: This project is a 6DOF bionic robotic arm with individually controlled fingers and a 360° rotating base, operated through real-time hand tracking. I began building it in November 2023, at age 13, starting with a simple 5DOF model using an Arduino Uno and 20kg servo motors. As the project advanced, I added full base rotation, upgraded to a Raspberry Pi with an external servo driver, and solved issues like power distribution, servo lag, and signal noise. I designed a wearable glove with flex sensors and motion tracking (using an accelerometer and gyroscope) to control the arm myself through hand movements. The glove sends movement data to the Pi, which converts it into servo commands, allowing the arm to mimic natural hand gestures like gripping, rotating, and placing objects. This project taught me key concepts in electronics, coding, power systems, and biomechanics. It remains in development, with planned upgrades including wireless communication, stronger grip, and improved gesture recognition.
